mission: Reveal information that is already in the photograph — light, color, structure, and research-informed animal vision simulations — without inventing UV, IR, or thermal signals.
promise: Look again — light, color, structure, and animal vision already waiting in your photograph.

epistemicLabels.label: MEASURED
epistemicLabels.meaning: Taken from values present in the file or EXIF when available.

epistemicLabels.label: COMPUTED
epistemicLabels.meaning: Derived mathematically from RGB pixel values in the photograph.

epistemicLabels.label: SIMULATED
epistemicLabels.meaning: A human-viewable approximation grounded in research, not a claim of exact non-human experience.

epistemicLabels.label: INFERRED
epistemicLabels.meaning: Estimated from visual cues; not directly measured.

epistemicLabels.label: UNAVAILABLE
epistemicLabels.meaning: The required signal was not captured in this RGB photograph.

spectralUnavailable.title: Ultraviolet
spectralUnavailable.summary: Ordinary RGB photographs do not contain ultraviolet reflectance. Waypoint will not invent UV nectar guides or UV plumage patterns into your image.

spectralUnavailable.title: Near-infrared
spectralUnavailable.summary: Stock cameras block most near-infrared. Creative IR looks are not offered as if they were captured IR.

spectralUnavailable.title: Thermal
spectralUnavailable.summary: Thermal radiance is a different measurement. RGB luminance is not heat.

spectralUnavailable.title: Polarization
spectralUnavailable.summary: Polarization requires dedicated capture. It is not recoverable from a standard photograph.

spectralUnavailable.title: Hyperspectral
spectralUnavailable.summary: Hyperspectral bands beyond RGB are not present in this file.

pillars.name: Light
pillars.question: Where is light concentrated, and how is tonal information distributed?

views.name: Photograph
views.what: The photograph you opened — the reference for every comparison.
views.why: Discovery starts from what the camera actually recorded in visible light.
views.measured: Decoded RGB pixels from the selected source (Original or Waypoint Edit).

views.name: Luminance
views.what: A grayscale map of relative luminance (Rec. 709 weights on linearized sRGB).
views.why: Human vision and photography both lean on luminance structure more than hue alone.
views.measured: Per-pixel Y computed from sRGB → linear → Rec. 709 luminance.

views.name: Tonal structure
views.what: Zones classified from the luminance histogram of this JPEG/PNG — not RAW recovery.
views.why: Shows where detail is compressed versus open, within what this file contains.
views.measured: Luminance histogram bins; clipped highlights counted from near-255 samples.

views.name: Light concentration
views.what: A soft map emphasizing regions that contribute most of the scene’s bright energy.
views.why: Helps you notice sky dominance, specular water, or bright openings you may overlook.
views.measured: Spatial weighting of high-luminance pixels on a downsampled analysis grid.

pillars.name: Color
pillars.question: How do color families and relationships organize this landscape?

views.name: Photograph
views.why: Color exploration is relative to what was actually recorded.

views.name: Color families
views.short: Dominant hue families in the frame.
views.what: A posterized reading of major hue families by pixel share — observation, not a palette product.
views.why: Makes the scene’s chromatic structure easier to notice at a glance.
views.measured: Hue histogram in HSL space with saturation/value gates.

views.name: Warm / cool
views.what: A split view tinting warm and cool regions for comparison.
views.why: Temperature relationships often organize outdoor light more than we consciously register.
views.measured: Per-pixel warm/cool classification from hue angle.

views.name: Saturation
views.short: Where chroma is strong or quiet.
views.what: A map of relative saturation; low-chroma areas stay muted.
views.why: Chromatic accents (understory, flowers, signs) often hide in overall green or brown scenes.

pillars.name: Structure
pillars.question: What are the bones of this photograph — edges, texture, and form?

views.name: Photograph
views.why: Structure views are overlays on real detail, not invented geometry.

views.name: Edge density
views.what: A Sobel magnitude map — brighter means stronger local edge energy.
views.why: Edge density often concentrates in foliage, shoreline, or built edges you skim past.

views.name: Texture
views.what: Local luminance variance — a proxy for texture richness, not a material classifier.
views.why: Helps separate smooth sky/water from busy vegetation or ground cover.

views.name: Local contrast
views.what: How strongly each neighborhood differs from its local mean.
views.why: Local contrast often reveals form when global contrast looks flat.
views.measured: Absolute deviation from local mean luminance.

views.name: Estimated depth
views.what: A soft near/far estimate from haze and vertical position cues — not a depth map from stereo or LiDAR.
views.why: Useful as a reading aid; never treat as measured distance.
views.measured: Heuristic from relative luminance haze and image Y position (INFERRED).

pillars.name: Animal Vision
pillars.question: How might selected differences appear under another visual system?

views.name: Human (source)
views.short: Your RGB photograph as humans view it on this display.
views.what: The source photograph on a human RGB display.

views.name: White-tailed deer
views.what: A research-informed dichromatic remap — not exact deer subjective vision.
views.why: Red–green separation collapses in ways that matter for trail markers, berries, and clothing.
views.measured: LMS projection onto a deer-like dichromat plane (SIMULATED).

views.name: Canine
views.what: A research-informed dichromatic remap for dog/canid cone assumptions.
views.why: Shows which color contrasts remain informative versus collapsed.
views.measured: LMS projection onto a canine-like dichromat plane (SIMULATED).

views.name: Bee / UV
views.what: Educational state: this photograph cannot reconstruct ultraviolet flower patterns.
views.why: Honesty beats inventing nectar guides the camera never measured.
views.measured: No UV channel in source — UNAVAILABLE.

views.name: Bird / UV
views.short: Bird UV deferred — UNAVAILABLE from RGB.
views.what: Many birds sense UV; ordinary RGB files do not record it. Mode deferred rather than faked.
views.why: Deferring weak models protects scientific trust.
views.measured: No UV channel in source — UNAVAILABLE.
